runs.summary: Firecrawl discovery worked again after fixing the map-link shaping bug, but usable results only came from a reduced-limit rerun because the default query budget exhausted credits and rate limits. The reduced Firecrawl pool still surfaced direct-operator pages first; after live verification, Beatrice remained the only strict shortlist survivor. Later NYBits supplements added three real 2BR/2BA East Village monitor candidates plus several worthwhile 1BR monitor rows led by 250 Mott, Chelsea Centro, CD 280, StuyTown, and Ohm, but none had the complete floor-plan / must-have certainty needed to displace Beatrice or create a new Track B shortlist row.
runs.notes: This run began with Firecrawl discovery. The original required run against data/firecrawl-discovery/2026-05-18.json failed before output because discover-apartments-firecrawl.mjs assumed map links were strings. After patching the script to accept Firecrawl link objects, a reduced-limit post-fix rerun (searchLimit=1, mapLimit=2) produced the only usable Firecrawl candidate pool today and was copied into the date-specific discovery file after later full reruns exhausted credits. Verification then started from the Firecrawl direct-operator candidates (AVA High Line, 777 6th Avenue, 208 West 23rd Street) before supplementing with fresh opened-page StreetEasy and Brodsky unit pages. After that, user-requested NYBits passes added several no-fee East Village / Chelsea / NoLiTa leads across both 2BR and 1BR searches; the worthwhile ones were page-verified and merged here as additional monitor or excluded rows.
sourcesSearched: Firecrawl balanced query set with reduced-limit post-fix rerun
blindSpots: The original Firecrawl run crashed on 2026-05-18 because map links came back as objects rather than bare URL strings; this was fixed in scripts/discover-apartments-firecrawl.mjs during the run.

The full post-fix Firecrawl rerun still degraded because the current plan exhausted credits on search queries (402) and hit map rate limits (429), so the usable discovery pool came from the reduced-limit rerun with searchLimit=1 and mapLimit=2.

Firecrawl query set used the balanced 18-query pack covering 1BR, 2BR/2BA, and true 3BR/3BA discovery plus StreetEasy/Zillow/Apartments.com/RentHop site queries; mapped roots were Equity Apartments, Avalon Communities, Brodsky, Stonehenge NYC, Rockrose, EVE NYC, StuyTown / Beam Living, The Chelsea / Greystar, and Chelsea29.

AVA High Line exposed live building-level availability and media, but the accessible page did not expose clean current unit rows or move-in dates for specific 1BRs in a way that tied exact must-haves to a live unit.
Equity pages were Cloudflare-blocked from shell fetches, so verification relied on opened pages instead of raw curl output for Beatrice and 777 6th Avenue.
StreetEasy provided useful live unit pages, but several discovery leads were stale once opened or still omitted square footage and A/C/HVAC details.

NYBits was useful for finding additional no-fee broker rows, but many 9300 Realty East Village pages were 1-2 months old, repeated the same buildings in multiple unit variants, and still lacked square footage / floor plans, so the best ones stayed monitor-only.
Chelsea29 remained blocked behind Cloudflare and was not trustworthy enough to include beyond the blind-spot note.
